subject: HeliosAI sustained throughput degradation — executive update and next steps
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@heliosai.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: carter.ng@heliosai.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency on production realtime endpoints

Sergio / team,

We're seeing elevated tail latency and periodic timeouts on our realtime inference endpoint (v1.3) starting ~14:40 PDT. Error rate is small (~0.8% 5xx) but p95/p99 token latency spiked from ~110ms to 1.2s which is causing visible UI timeouts for customers.

We kicked traffic to a read-only canary and confirmed higher latency persists; request ID examples attached in the logs. Impact: a subset of interactive sessions timing out, some downstream retry storms. We have a customer meeting in 90 mins and need an exec-level note + ETA. Can Redwood stand up a bridge and confirm whether this is an RL/serving runtime regression or infra (GPU scheduling)?

Thanks,
Dana Li
Head of Product Ops, HeliosAI

Attachments: helios-request-ids.txt (text)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Dana Li <dana.li@heliosai.com>, carter.ng@heliosai.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency on production realtime endpoints

Dana — thanks for the heads up and example IDs. We've opened a bridge and PagerDuty incident (PD-84211) and are mobilizing SRE + runtime on-call. Bridge details below: 
- Bridge (Zoom): https://zoom.us/j/bridge-helio-84211
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-84211
- Initial triage owners: Ben (serving runtime), Marissa (infra), Lauren (customer comms)

Immediate actions we're running now:
1) Verify canary vs prod config parity and hotfix any kernel/quantization option mismatch.
2) Temporarily drain new sessions to a lighter model variant (v1.2-q4_0) to reduce memory/kv-cache pressure while preserving throughput.
3) Enable detailed per-request tracing for the next 30m (we'll redact payloads) and upload logs to the shared Drive folder.

I'll post an executive-facing blurb for your meeting within 20 minutes. Please add any customer-side traces to the Drive link so we can correlate.

- Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Dana Li <dana.li@heliosai.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High tail latency on production realtime endpoints — executive summary

Dana —

Quick executive summary you can share in the meeting: 

Impact: Intermittent high p95/p99 token latency and a small number of 5xx errors impacting interactive sessions since ~14:40 PDT. We estimate ~3–5% of requests experienced degraded latency at peak; error rate ~0.8%. No data loss reported.

Cause (initial): We are investigating a likely interaction between a recent runtime kernel selection change and high-concurrency KV cache pressure leading to serialization delays in the inference runtime. Our infra team is also validating underlying GPU scheduling and host kernel telemetry.

Actions taken: 
- Opened incident PD-84211 and stood up a bridge with SRE and runtime engineers.
- Shifted new sessions to a lighter model variant (v1.2-q4_0) as an immediate mitigation to reduce memory and cache contention.
- Enabled per-request tracing and increased sampling for the affected endpoints.

Next steps and ETA: 
- Short-term (30–90 min): stabilize latency by traffic shift and hotfix any kernel mismatch (target: 80% baseline p95 within 30–60m).
- Medium-term (today): full root-cause analysis and rollback plan or forward-fix depending on kernel compatibility (target: action plan within 6 hours).

Compensation: We will propose a goodwill credit if SLA thresholds were breached; we'll follow up postmortem with final credit calculation.

I'll remain on the bridge and will update you every 30 minutes.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Dana Li <dana.li@heliosai.com>, carter.ng@heliosai.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency on production realtime endpoints — status update

Dana — quick status update from the bridge: 
- Mitigation executed: traffic is now routing 84% of new interactive sessions to v1.2-q4_0 (lighter quant) and legacy routes remain for existing sessions. Early metrics show p95 dropped from 1.2s to ~220ms after the shift.
- Identified probable root cause: a default kernel selector path enabled last week that performs poorly under high concurrent prefix reuse. We're testing a runtime patch to force the fallback kernel for affected model shapes; if tests pass we'll stage the patch to a small cluster in ~45 minutes.
- Postmortem draft (internal) uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Helios-Incident-20270410 (file: postmortem-draft-v1.docx).

Customer asks we will address: clear timeline for permanent fix, postmortem with action items, and a proposed credit if SLA impacted. We'll provide specific timelines in the next update.

Attachments on bridge: bridge-log-1612.txt (traces), workflow-run-424.json (sampling).

— Sergio
From: Dana Li <dana.li@heliosai.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: carter.ng@heliosai.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High tail latency on production realtime endpoints — thank you

Sergio / team — thank you for the quick response and the clear mitigation path. The meeting went well; customers appreciated the transparency. Two quick asks: 
1) Please share the postmortem with high-level timeline and the engineering action items when the draft is ready. We need that for our audit and for our CTO.
2) Can we get a provisional estimate of potential SLA credit range so we can communicate to procurement?

Appreciate the rapid support.

— Dana
Head of Product Ops, HeliosAI
